thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#INC-34871 - inference-service-queue-delay > 250s in us-west-2. observed queue length 12k, 95p latency 340s. alert rule: autoscaler_queue_depth_alert

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty page: incident INC-34871 opened, priority P1. triggered by alerting rule 'autoscaler_queue_depth_alert'. paging rotation: Alex (oncall) -> Maya (sre).

Alex (oncall): ack. I'm on it. pinging Maya.

Maya (sre): ack. looking. first glance: control-plane reports no new replicas for the inference worker sets for last 18m. HPA shows desired=5 current=5, queue backlog increasing.

Alex (oncall): any PD/ops runbooks?

Maya (sre): runbook: https://console.internal/redwood/runbooks/autoscaler-queue.md - main steps: check HPA metrics, check kubeapi quota, check spot/instance bot.

Jon (runtime): jumping in. Noticed a spike in cold-start miss rate earlier. Could be KV-cache churn causing request fanout and small CPU signals. Posting relevant logs:
```
[2026-03-15T10:03:12Z] inference-worker-5 ERROR prefix_cache_miss key=abc123
[2026-03-15T10:03:15Z] autoscaler INFO scale_decision: metric=cpu target=60% -> no-scale (avg 12%) reason=low-cpu
[2026-03-15T10:05:48Z] queue_monitor WARN backlog=9842 ingress_rate=220/s
```

Ryan (support): Customer reports: several customers seeing 504s and timeouts on /v1/generate. We have open support tickets: #RD-4283, #RD-4284. Marking impact: high.

Linda (prod-eng): Is the autoscaler using CPU? Our inference queue backlog should be driving scale. If metrics are CPU-only, that explains no scale.

Maya (sre): confirmed: HPA for inference-worker is CPU-based. There's a new rollout from last week that changed metric config for a subset of clusters (config drift).

Alex (oncall): action plan: 1) manually scale up worker pool to reduce backlog, 2) switch HPA metric to queue_depth for quick mitigation, 3) investigate why rollout changed metric. Who can apply manual scale?

Jon (runtime): I can run a manual scale. Doing: `kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-worker --replicas=20 --context=us-west-2`

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty note added: "Manual scale initiated by Jon (runtime)"

Jon (runtime): scale command succeeded. new replicas coming up: 15 -> 20. watching pods.

Maya (sre): checking metrics now. queue length dropping from 12k -> 6.8k in 3m. 95p latency down to 160s. still degraded but trending good.

Alex (oncall): good. set tentative incident status to "mitigating". Notify support and customers. Ryan, can you post an interim update?

Ryan (support): Posted to customers on status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-34871 - "We're seeing increased inference times in us-west-2; mitigation in progress; temporary capacity added."

Linda (prod-eng): For a more durable fix we should revert the config drift. I can push a config patch to restore queue-based HPA. Will prepare PR.

Maya (sre): Suggest we also change autoscaler policy to consider inflight queue depth metric (queue_length*weight) and add a short-term override to scale faster (min_replicas bumped).

Jon (runtime): Applied a temporary HPA patch to use custom metric queue_length for us-west-2: `kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2beta2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-worker
  namespace: inference
spec:
  minReplicas: 10
  maxReplicas: 100
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: queue_length
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: 200
EOF`

Maya (sre): HPA change rolled. New desired replicas recalculating -> desired=50 (based on queue). Autoscaler controller will handle spinups.

Alex (oncall): any blockers for adding replicas? quotas or cloud limits?

Jon (runtime): We're hitting spot pool depletion in us-west-2 AZ-a. Fallback to on-demand available but will cost more. We have capacity in us-west-2 AZ-b and us-east-1. Can we allow cross-AZ scheduling?

Maya (sre): kube-scheduler refusing some pods due to PodAntiAffinity and AZ constraints from recent policy change. Quick fix: remove strict anti-affinity for inference-worker to allow AZ-b scheduling. Applying patch now.

Jon (runtime): anti-affinity relaxed. pods can schedule in AZ-b. New nodes requested.

Maya (sre): backlog dropped to 2.1k, 95p latency 48s. Customer impact reduced substantially.

Ryan (support): Updating support tickets and customers: "We added temporary capacity and an HPA override; latency improving. We'll follow up with root cause and permanent fix."

Linda (prod-eng): PR opened to revert metric drift and add test to prevent regressions: https://git.internal/redwood/inference-configs/pull/987. Also adding alert to detect HPA metric mismatch.

Alex (oncall): timeline and actions for post-incident: 1) keep HPA queue metric for 1 hour until queue drained, 2) monitor cost impact, 3) root-cause: identify rollout that changed metric; block future rollouts without canary, 4) follow-up postmortem.

Maya (sre): I'm going to keep the page open for 60m and monitor. If metrics stable, we can scale down gracefully.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident update: INC-34871 status changed to acknowledged -> mitigated (manual actions in place).

Alex (oncall): handing off monitoring to Maya for the next rotation. Maya, you're the primary for the next 40m. I'll update the ops channel and escalate to eng oncall-leads if anything regresses.

Maya (sre): ack handoff. Logging all commands and timestamps to the incident doc.

Jon (runtime): note: we should also add queue_length as a signal to the global autoscaler config; I'll file a follow-up ticket.

Ryan (support): Closing customer interim message; will wait for postmortem to add RCA.

Alex (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll create the postmortem draft and assign owners: Linda for configuration drift RCA, Jon for scheduler/spot analysis, Maya for mitigation timelines.

Maya (sre): incident channel left open. moving to observation mode. :eyes:
